design_rationale:
WORKLOG — pass_protection_desk task 0 (root problem: insure_ext_claim_settlement)

STEP 0. DRAW AND SCOPE SNAPSHOT.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/tasks/pass_protection_desk --tasks 2 printed
{"task": 0, "key": "ski_resort_operator/pass_protection_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1,
"problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]} and {"task": 1, ..., "prerequisite_problems": 2,
"problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 4]}. So this task is a two-problem tree — one root plus
exactly one prerequisite problem — and each of its two computations declares exactly six factors.
Nothing was occupied when this task was claimed (it is the first task of the difficulty). This task
claims insure_ext_amendment_reprice (subject insure_amend, the household's own confirmation) and
insure_ext_claim_settlement (subject insure_claim_payment). Left for task 1: the premium
presentation on a live plan (insure_premium_charge), the charge raised when a plan is given up
(insure_fee_charge) and what comes back when it is given up (insure_cancel) — three untouched
subjects, three untouched target tools, enough for its drawn three-problem tree. No base policy is
consumed exclusively: insure_eligibility_and_quote and insure_premium_terms are cited here as
lineage and remain available to task 1 as lineage for other subjects.

DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal: the household wants the claim they made on the pass protection settled
and the money paid out. Scored core parameter: the payout, 547.42 USD. Between the goal and
that number the policy puts one problem the customer never mentions: the plan's own rule fixes what
a claim pays against the value the plan carries as covered, and it says outright that the figure is
worked out only once that covered value stands at the price the covered holding's own record shows.
The records show it does not — the plan carries 1149.00 while the pass record carries 1879.00 — and
only the household itself can confirm the change to its own plan, which also reprices the premium.
So the tree is: confirm the plan's covered value and its repriced premium (the household's own
write), then settle the claim. Breadth: the payout is decided in parallel by the papers on the claim
(which share applies, which day the claim is measured from), by the covered pass's own tier (the days
the value is spread across), by the pass's scan history, by the resort credit standing on the pass
account and by the instalment its payment method refused — five independent stretches of record,
three of them in another difficulty's product.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST. Nothing here can be reached by picking a tool: both writes are hidden and
both are named only by the policy. The difficulty is in reading out of the settlement rule that it
waits on a record-visible state, checking that state against two different products' records, seeing
that only the household can put it right, and then reconciling five stretches of ledger to a cent. An
agent who settles the claim straight away books 207.90 instead of 547.42; an agent
who reads only the computation document and none of the factor documents books 919.20.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Write 1 — subject insure_amend. The only base policy whose subject intersects insure_amend is
insure_eligibility_and_quote; its single structured gate, within_purchase_window, applies_to
insure_quote alone and therefore does not gate this write, so the policy enters
solvability_contract as policy_scope. Its inherited boundaries are honoured all the same: the plan
is written over a holding that exists on the household account (b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62) and belongs to a product
line the plan covers (covered_product_category passes, and Season Pass Protection Plus covers
passes); the covered value used is the price committed to on the covered holding as the collective's
record shows it (passes_holdings.price_paid_usd = 1879.00), not as the household recalls it — the
household is never asked for it; and 1879.00 falls between the plan's smallest and largest covered
values (559.00 and 2649.00). Amendment is allowed on this tier (amendment_allowed true). No time
gate is in play on this write, so temporal_feasibility is empty for it.
Write 2 — subject insure_claim_payment. The only base policy whose subject intersects it is
insure_claim_assessment, and its gate payout_state applies: "The payout is made only while the plan
record stands in the claim_open or claim_settled state, and it draws down the benefit left for the
rest of the season." At frozen_time the plan stands claim_open (system record, pre-action), so the
gate holds; the gate's correlation key insure_holdings.protection_plan_id binds to the call's
protection_plan_id argument. The claim-intake gates (notice period, papers on record) apply to
insure_claim_open and insure_document_receive, neither of which this task writes; both are
nevertheless satisfied in the world (claim made 2027-01-06 on an event of the first week of January,
well inside the plan's 45 notice days counted from cover beginning, and documents_complete true with
all three papers the plan requires standing accepted). No time gate applies to this write either.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is protection plan e47b2f60-8c15-4d93-a2e7-6b0f9c3a1d58 — one plan, one season
(2026-27), written over exactly one holding, pass b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62. Every aggregate is correlated by that
plan id or by that pass id: the papers counted are insure_ledger rows carrying this protection plan
id; the cover left is this plan's coverage-load entries less this plan's payouts; the scans, the
credit and the refused instalment are passes_ledger rows carrying pass_id b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62, never the
household at large. The household's second pass, 51a8d0c7-6e39-4b72-9f84-2a6c1d8b4e07 (Nila's Midweek Pass), is the deliberate
exclusion: its two scans, its two instalment charges and its plan opening sit on the same household
account, and only the household-wide adjustment in the repricing counts it (it counts pass openings
across the household by design, which is the one rule stated in household terms). The payout entry
written carries related_event_id = 76a2f0c9-4b83-4e17-95d0-3c8b1e6a9f52, the entry recording the accepted letter from the
former employer, so the payout points back to the single paper it was assessed from rather than to
the claim at large; the earlier employer letter d31e6b48-0c95-4a73-8f26-5b9d7c4a2e01 was recorded illegible and is not it.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root problem: insure_ext_claim_settlement (target tool settle_protection_claim_ed51c2df, owner
agent). Prerequisite problem: insure_ext_amendment_reprice (target tool
confirm_plan_value_amendment_50d33fe4, owner user — the household's own write, handed over by the
agent). One edge, kind value_input, gate: the covered_value binding of the settlement compute.
Form: state. Prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the settlement rule: "What a claim pays is
worked out only after the value the plan carries as covered stands at the price the covered holding's
own record shows, since what is paid is measured against the value the plan covers." Four-point
test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result (what a claim
pays) to what it waits on; (2) the waited-on side is a record-visible state — the covered value
carried on the plan set against the price on the covered holding's record — and names no action, no
performer and no tool; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token and no row id;
(4) its strength is exactly the edge's: a hard "only after", scoped to the covered value of this plan
alone. Exactly one write in this difficulty brings that state about: confirm_plan_value_amendment_50d33fe4
is the only action that writes insure_holdings.covered_value_usd (the other four policies write
premium, fee, payout and cancellation entries), so the reader can resolve the hop without being told.
Derivation: the sentence says the payout waits on the covered value standing at the covered holding's
price; the records show 1149.00 against 1879.00; the repricing policy's own rule says a plan whose
covered value is brought onto the price the covered holding's record shows has its premium worked
out afresh, and its result is confirmed by the household — so the one action that restores the state
is that confirmation. Unresolved at frozen_time: initial_state.insure_holdings.e47b2f60-8c15-4d93-a2e7-6b0f9c3a1d58.covered_value_usd
= 1149.00 while initial_state.passes_holdings.b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62.price_paid_usd = 1879.00, the gap left by the
move up of tier recorded on 2026-12-06 (pass account entry 2b7e0d46-9a53-4f18-97c6-4d1b8e5a0f37, 730.00). Flips to true when
the confirmation writes covered_value_usd = 1879.00. Topological order: repricing, then settlement;
there are no parallel edges to reorder. Deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skipping the
confirmation leaves the settlement computing 207.90 instead of 547.42. The
customer never mentions any of it — user_scenario says nothing about the pass having moved up a
tier, about the plan's covered value, or about a change to the plan; her only line on the subject is
a passive one that fires after the agent has explained it. The tool layer blocks nothing: both
function bodies in task_tools.py are a single ctx.update / ctx.create with no lookup of the other
problem's state and no refusal path.

FACTOR CARD — insure_ext_amendment_reprice (six factors, four parameter and two method).
1. rate_standing (parameter, cross-difficulty passes, multi-source). Tiers: an instalment refused on
   the covered holding's account in the season and the plan not out of force for non-payment -> the
   plan's rate loaded by the arrears loading; no refused instalment and no payout on the plan this
   season -> the plan's rate relieved by the claim-free relief; otherwise the plan's own rate. This
   world: pass account entry 74d1f3a9-0c68-4b25-8fa3-2e6d9c1b5074 is an instalment the payment method refused on 2026-12-15
   (expired card, 191.50), so the rate is 7.5 rather than the plan's 6.5. Baseline reading (the
   plan's own rate) would give 102.87 instead of 117.46.
2. age_adjustment (parameter, cross-difficulty passes). Tiers: child, youth or teen age band -> the
   junior step; senior or super-senior -> the senior step; otherwise nothing. This world:
   passes_holdings.b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62.age_band = teen, so the junior step applies. Baseline (no adjustment)
   gives 125.01.
3. household_adjustment (parameter, cross-difficulty passes). Tiers: the household's pass accounts
   carry the opening price entry of three or more passes for the season -> the three-pass step; two
   -> the two-pass step; otherwise nothing. This world: two openings (3f0a6b12-7d84-4c95-9e26-0a7b5d3c8e11 for b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62,
   d80f2b57-1a94-4e6c-9037-6b5d8c2a4f19 for 51a8d0c7-6e39-4b72-9f84-2a6c1d8b4e07), so the two-pass step. Baseline gives
   121.24.
4. standing_adjustment (parameter, cross-difficulty passes). Tiers: the covered holding renewed from
   a previous season -> the renewal step; carried forward -> the carry-forward step; otherwise
   nothing. This world: renewal_source = renewal. Baseline gives 122.50.
5. change_anchor (method, cross-difficulty passes). Tiers: an entry for a move up of tier standing on
   the covered holding's account for the season -> the change takes effect from the day that entry
   was raised; no such entry -> from the day the change is recorded; otherwise from the day cover
   began. This world: 2b7e0d46-9a53-4f18-97c6-4d1b8e5a0f37 dated 2026-12-06, so the change runs from 2026-12-06. Baseline (the
   day cover began) gives 122.61.
6. difference_spread (method, cross-difficulty passes, multi-source). Tiers: a move-up entry on the
   covered holding's account and the premium collected alongside that holding's instalments -> the
   difference is spread over the days of cover still to come as a share of the whole term; no move-up
   entry and the premium collected alongside instalments -> spread evenly over the instalments still
   to fall; otherwise the whole difference at once. This world: the move-up entry stands and Season
   Pass Protection Plus is collected with the holding's instalments, so 133 of 149 days.
   Baseline (the whole difference at once) gives 122.61.
   Near-miss on this computation: the household's other pass 51a8d0c7-6e39-4b72-9f84-2a6c1d8b4e07 carries its own instalment
   charges and scans; none of them may enter the covered-holding aggregates, which are all filtered
   to pass b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62, and only the household-wide adjustment counts across both. Whole-baseline
   reading of the computation document alone: 122.14, against gold 117.46.

FACTOR CARD — insure_ext_claim_settlement (six factors, three parameter and three method).
1. peril_share (parameter, multi-source). Tiers: an accepted letter from the former employer and a
   claim made on loss of employment -> the plan's share for loss of employment; accepted proof of a
   permanent move and a claim on a permanent move -> the plan's share for a permanent move;
   otherwise the plan's medical share. This world: 76a2f0c9-4b83-4e17-95d0-3c8b1e6a9f52 is an accepted employer letter and
   the plan's claim_reason is job_loss, so 70 rather than the medical 80. Baseline gives
   672.27.
2. measuring_day (method). Tiers: a paper accepted on the claim reaching the collective after the day
   the claim was made -> the claim is measured from the day the last accepted paper arrived; every
   accepted paper on or before that day -> from the day the claim was made; no accepted paper at all
   -> from the day cover began. This world: the claim was made 2027-01-06 and the accepted employer
   letter arrived 2027-01-09, so the claim is measured from 2027-01-09. Baseline gives
   919.20.
3. spread_span (method). Tiers: cover beginning on or before the day the season opened and the
   plan's waiting period ending after cover began -> the days from the first day of the season the
   plan covers to its last; cover beginning after the season opened -> the days from cover beginning
   to cover ending; otherwise the days from the day the waiting period ended to the day cover is due
   to end. Every tier is a span of calendar days, the same kind of day the numerator counts, so the
   proportion can never exceed one. This world: cover began 2026-11-20, the day the season opened,
   and the waiting period ended 2026-11-30, so the span is 149. Baseline (139 days from the waiting
   period's end to the end of cover) gives 610.30.
4. value_at_risk_measure (method, cross-difficulty passes). Tiers: scans on the covered holding's
   account and cover beginning on or before the season opening -> the covered value in proportion to
   the days of the season still to come; scans and cover beginning later -> the covered value less
   the tier's day-use deduction for each day scanned; no scans -> the whole covered value. This
   world: five scans on b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62 and cover beginning on the opening day, so 1879.00 x 99 / 149 =
   1248.46, under the ceiling of the value the plan covers that the same tier states. Baseline gives
   919.20.
5. credit_offset (parameter, cross-difficulty passes). Tiers: credit issued in the season for the
   pass being given up -> the whole of it set against; no such credit but credit issued in recovery
   of service -> the whole of that set against; otherwise nothing. This world: 1c8d7a95-4e20-4f63-98b1-6a3c5d0e7f82, 85.00
   issued in recovery of service on 2026-12-28, and no cancellation credit. Baseline gives
   632.42.
6. holding_arrears_offset (parameter, cross-difficulty passes). Tiers: an instalment the payment
   method refused on the covered holding's account in the season -> the amount so refused set
   against; no refusal but a balance still to be collected -> that balance set against; otherwise
   nothing. This world: 74d1f3a9-0c68-4b25-8fa3-2e6d9c1b5074, 191.50 refused. Baseline gives
   738.92.
   Near-miss on this computation: the first employer letter d31e6b48-0c95-4a73-8f26-5b9d7c4a2e01 was recorded illegible on
   2027-01-07; counting it would move the day the claim is measured from and, if it were treated as
   accepted, nothing else — the rule counts only accepted papers, and the accepted one is dated
   2027-01-09. The medical certificate 8c05a7d3-9f41-4b26-a3e8-1d6c2b0f5e97 stands accepted (the plan's paper pack requires
   one) but the share still follows what the claim was made on, not what papers happen to be on file.
   Whole-baseline reading of the computation document alone: 919.20, against gold
   547.42. The plan's per-claim cap (1600.00) and the cover left on the plan (919.20) are
   plumbing rather than factors here: both are above the gold figure, so neither binds, and every one
   of the six factors moves the scored number.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
customers 6c1d9f2a-4b77-4a1e-9c30-1f5b8e2d7a44: the household; its mobile number is the only locator the caller offers, and its
date of birth and postal code are the two credentials the verification tool needs. passes_holdings
b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62: the covered holding — its price_paid_usd is the value the whole task turns on, its
age_band decides the age adjustment, its renewal_source the standing adjustment, its variant the
day-use deduction, its installment_balance_usd the fall-through of the arrears offset. passes_holdings 51a8d0c7-6e39-4b72-9f84-2a6c1d8b4e07: the second pass — without it the household adjustment
falls to nothing and the repricing changes; its own ledger rows are the near-miss for every
covered-holding aggregate. passes_ledger: the plan opening of each pass (the household adjustment),
three instalment charges and the refusal 74d1f3a9-0c68-4b25-8fa3-2e6d9c1b5074 (the rate loading and the arrears offset), the
late fee that answers the refusal (realism and the balance), the move-up charge 2b7e0d46-9a53-4f18-97c6-4d1b8e5a0f37 (the day
the change takes effect and the spread), the service-recovery credit 1c8d7a95-4e20-4f63-98b1-6a3c5d0e7f82 (the credit offset)
and five scans on b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62 (the value at risk). Remove any one of them and the named factor falls
to its fall-through. insure_ledger: three premium charges and the three payments that matched them
(premium_balance_usd 0.00, and the reason the plan never lapsed although the pass instalment was
refused — the December premium was paid at the desk on 2026-12-16), the coverage load of 919.20 (the
cover left), and four paper entries (the share, the measuring day and the near-miss). There is no
stale cache in this task: insure_holdings.premium_balance_usd and benefit_remaining_usd both equal
the signed sum of their ledger deltas, and passes_holdings.installment_balance_usd equals
1149.00 + 730.00 + 35.00 - 383.00 = 1531.00, the price and fees booked less the two instalments that
cleared.

AUTOMATIC-CLAUSE CHECK. The insure automatic clauses are lapse on a premium instalment unpaid past
the grace period, expiry at the end of the season and closure once nothing is owed. None fires here:
every premium entry raised on the plan is matched by a payment, the season runs to 2027-04-18, and
the plan carries an open claim. On the passes side the refusal of 2026-12-15 is answered by the late
fee already booked; the pass tier's suspension threshold is more than one refusal, so no suspension
is owed and the pass stands active.

PERSONA DESIGN. Corinne is written as a tired, practical caller rather than an angry one: she states
the redundancy and what she wants once, gives the mobile number as the locator and holds the date of
birth and postal code back until asked, and refuses to recite figures ("you would rather they read it
off their own records"), which keeps every number in gold on the system side. She volunteers nothing
about the pass having moved up a tier or about the plan's covered value; her only contribution to the
prerequisite is the passive line that fires once the agent has explained that the plan has to be put
onto the right value and has handed the confirmation across. Her stopping condition is a natural
utterance event — the agent telling her the claim has been settled and the money is on its way — and
it answers the last gold action, asking for nothing beyond it. Every fact she offers is entailed by
the opening world: the claim she made (claim_opened_date 2027-01-06), the papers she sent in (the
entries of 2027-01-06, 2027-01-07 and 2027-01-09), the plan taken in October (purchased_date
2026-10-09) and Rohan being the insured. She does not date those papers or say which of them was
accepted: asked when the letter from the firm reached the collective she says she could not say
offhand and would rather they read it off their own record, so the day the claim is measured from and
the near-miss of the illegible letter are settled by the record alone and never pre-announced.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Turn by turn: she gives the mobile number, the agent finds the
household and verifies with two credentials she states; the plans and passes are read back; the
protection account and both pass accounts are read; the agent sees the covered value against the pass
price, explains the plan has to be brought onto it, unlocks the confirmation and hands it to her; she
makes it, and its receipt enters the shared transcript; the agent then settles the claim and tells
her. Every tool call is synchronous under one frozen_time; nothing waits on a diagnosis, a delivery,
a clearing, a review or a future date. Questions a real agent would ask that never enter gold — when
the job ended, whether anyone was ill, what the pass cost, whether she has a plan reference — all
have definite answers or a definite refusal in the persona.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Read the household, verify, read the plan, read both passes, read the protection
account and the pass accounts. Notice that the settlement rule waits on the covered value standing at
the covered holding's price, and that it does not. Work the repricing: the covered pass account
carries a refused instalment, so the rate is the plan's rate loaded by the arrears loading, 7.5; 7.5
per cent of 1879.00 is 140.93 inside the plan's premium bounds; the junior, two-pass and renewal
adjustments total minus thirteen per cent, applied once to 140.93, giving 122.61; the change takes
effect from the move-up entry of 2026-12-06, so 133 of the term's 149 days still to come; the
difference of 47.92 over the premium frozen on the plan is spread across them, giving
74.69 + 42.77 = 117.46. Hand that to the household with the covered value of 1879.00 for
confirmation. Then the settlement, on the world that confirmation leaves: an accepted employer letter
on a claim made on loss of employment gives the 70 per cent share; the claim is measured from
2027-01-09, the day the accepted letter arrived; 99 days still to come over the 149 days of the
season gives a value at risk of 1248.46, under the value the plan covers; 70 per cent of that is
873.92; the plan's
excess of 50.00, the 85.00 of service-recovery credit and the 191.50 refused instalment come off
afterwards, giving 547.42, which is below both the per-claim cap and the cover left. Book it
by the plan's payout method, resort_credit, against the accepted letter's entry.

VERIFICATION RUN. The handling-time recomputation was executed with the gate's own evaluator
(skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py machinery over this initial_state, the
repricing on the opening world and the settlement on the world after the confirmation write):
insure_ext_amendment_reprice -> 117.46; insure_ext_claim_settlement -> 547.42. Factor
sensitivity, one factor's baseline substituted at a time: rate_standing 102.87,
age_adjustment 125.01, household_adjustment
121.24, standing_adjustment 122.50,
change_anchor 122.61, difference_spread 122.61;
peril_share 672.27, measuring_day 919.20, spread_span
610.30, value_at_risk_measure 919.20,
credit_offset 632.42, holding_arrears_offset
738.92. Whole baselines: 122.14 and 919.20. Prerequisite
sensitivity: with the confirmation skipped, the settlement recomputes to 207.90. Every one
of the fourteen figures differs from its gold, so no factor and no edge is decorative.

TWO-WAY EQUIVALENCE (rule <-> compute). Forward: every binding that reads the world or makes a choice
carries a verbatim quotation in compute_basis — the aggregates (refused_instalments, household_passes,
instalments_charged, upgrade_entry_date, season_payouts, papers_employer, papers_relocation,
papers_accepted, last_paper_date, scan_days, cancellation_credit, service_credit,
refused_instalment_amount, benefit_left), the cross-category reads (new_covered_value,
covered_age_band, covered_standing, schedule_instalments, pass_operating_days, day_use_deduction,
holding_balance), every ladder binding, and the bounds, rounding and ordering bindings
(priced_premium, adjusted_premium, gross_allowed, result). Reverse sweep: each rule sentence carrying
a quantity, window, filter, branch, cap or rounding semantic is claimed by a binding — the bounds
sentence by priced_premium, the "added together into one total percentage ... adjusted once ... never
act successively" sentence by adjusted_premium, the spread sentence by spread_share, the "share is
taken of the value at risk first ... afterwards" sentence by gross_allowed, and the "brought down to
the per-claim cap and held to the cover left ... rounded to the cent" sentence by result. The acting
base is pinned in prose on both sides (the adjustments act on the bounded premium and never on the
premium frozen on the plan; the two deductions act on the product of share and value at risk and never
on the share). Rounding is pinned at the end and at no earlier step in the repricing, and to the cent
on the settled figure. Interval counting is stated where it matters: days still to come are counted
from the day the claim is measured from to the day cover is due to end, and the term from the day
cover began to the day cover is due to end.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected and this
worklog masked, and only the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, the finder returns and
the persona in view: the settlement document says the payout waits on the covered value standing at
the covered holding's price; the finders show 1149.00 against 1879.00; the repricing document is the
only one describing how a plan whose covered value is brought onto that price is priced, and its tool
is the household's own; so the order is forced. The figures then follow from the six factor documents
on each side, all of which are findable from the records the finders return (the refusal, the age
band, the two pass openings, the renewal source, the move-up entry, the scans, the credit, the
papers). Both the order and both figures come out the same as gold, and no second reading survives:
the covered value is fixed by the collective's record rather than the household's recollection, the
day the claim is measured from is fixed by the accepted paper rather than the illegible one, and the
payout method is fixed by the plan's own tier.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. gold_actions[7] carries the amendment write: its stage provenance
is performed_by_this_tool, its intent is the system's own record (the plan's covered value against the
pass price) since the policy is state_due, and its single base precondition is
insure_eligibility_and_quote at policy_scope. gold_actions[9] carries the payout: its intent is the
caller's own words, cited verbatim, since the policy is on_request; its discriminator is the phrase
"settle the claim on my son's pass protection"; its base precondition is
insure_claim_assessment.payout_state, evidenced by the plan row's protection_plan_id, status and
benefit_remaining_usd, with the gate's correlation key bound to the call's protection_plan_id
argument. temporal_feasibility is empty because neither write is governed by a time gate.
seed_consistency covers the plan row and all twelve protection account entries.


REVISION 2 — items closed from the source-layer policy-task audit (round 1 report:
env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/audits/policy_task/pass_protection_desk/). Symptom -> root cause -> change ->
re-run result, item by item; every change is in the charter or this task's own files.

F-RED-3 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, charter-global; bears on this task's root problem). Symptom: the
spread_span tier that applied divided a count of calendar days still to come by a count of operating
days the covered tier admits the holder on, so on a Four-Day Flex or Midweek pass the value at risk
came out above the whole value the plan covers (the audit's own figures: 10,370.25 on a 419.00 pass;
875.90 on a 629.00 pass). Root cause: a unit mismatch inside one tier — the numerator was fixed as
calendar days while the denominator was an operating-day allowance. Change: every tier of spread_span
is now a span of calendar days — the days of the season, the days from cover beginning to cover
ending, or the days from the waiting period's end to cover ending — so the two sides of the ratio
count the same kind of day; and the tier of value_at_risk_measure that takes the proportion now
states and applies a ceiling, "never more than the value the plan covers", which closes the shape for
every tier at once. Re-run: the Four-Day Flex case gives 419.00 x 99 / 149 = 278.38, below the pass
price, and the Midweek case 629.00 x 149 / 149 = 629.00, exactly the price and never above it. On
this task's world the span moves from 150 to 149 and the scored payout moves from 541.60 to
547.42; the tier taken, the tree, the edge and every factor's weight are unchanged, and the
six factor sensitivities were recomputed and all still differ from gold.

OBS-7 (covered value not re-bounded after the reprice). Change: the repricing rule and its compute now
take the price the covered holding's record shows as the new covered value only where it falls between
the plan's smallest and largest covered values, and otherwise leave the value the plan already covers
standing; the sentence is part of the baseline paragraph, and holding_price / new_covered_value carry
it in compute. Re-run: 1879.00 is inside Plus's 559.00-2649.00 band, so this task's repriced premium

OBS-9 (two unreachable tier-value collisions in peril_share on tiers that exclude the peril) and base

charter paid a claim on a peril the plan's own covered list does not name — the audit's case, Season
Pass Protection Plus with a claim made on bereavement, paid 919.20 where base pays nothing, and

added an overwrite entry that named the wrong base sentence. It declared superseded base's "A

this policy also requires an accepted paper, was already inside overwrite[0]'s superseded clause,
"The amount allowed is the plan's benefit share for the event claimed on...", so no second entry was
ever needed. Change: that overwrite entry is withdrawn, so base's covered-events sentence is
inherited unmodified again; and the gate it carries is stated and implemented in this policy's own
terms — the rule now says "Nothing is paid on a claim made on a peril the plan does not cover, the
events a plan pays out on being the ones its own list of covered perils names", the exclusion
sentence gains "so that an exclusion beats a cover wherever a peril stands in both lists", and
compute carries peril_covered alongside excluded_claim with result refusing on either. Re-run: the
audit's own case now pays 0.00, exactly what base gives; swept over all six plan tiers by all seven
peril values of the claim-reason enum, extended and base agree on every one of the 42 pairs,
including the eleven perils that stand in neither list. On this task's world claim_reason is

user_scenario:
You are Corinne Dhaliwal, forty-five, a project manager in Boulder who has skied
Granite Ridge since her twenties and now buys passes for the two teenagers as well. You are calling
the guest services centre on a Tuesday morning with the laptop open and the kettle on, and you sound
tired rather than cross: in the first week of January the firm you had worked at for eleven years let
you go with the rest of the analytics team, and the season has stopped being something you can think
about lightly. You put the claim in on the pass protection you took out in October over Rohan's
season pass, you sent in the papers they asked for, and you have heard nothing since. What you want from this call, in your own
words, is for someone to settle the claim on my son's pass protection and tell you what actually
comes back to you. You are happy for the agent to do whatever they can do on their side without
asking you first, and you say so if they check; anything that needs you to agree to it yourself, you
will do while you are on the line rather than call back later.

You give your mobile number as 3035550518 when the agent asks how to find the household, and you
have the account details to hand if they need more: your date of birth is 1981-07-09 and the home
postal code on the account is 80305. You will read either of those out if you are asked for them,
and you will give your email as corinne.dhaliwal@summitmail.com or your passholder number as
GR45013308 if the agent would rather have those instead. You do not know any reference numbers for
the protection plan itself and you say so if you are asked for one; you tell the agent to look it up
under the household. Rohan is the one the pass and the plan are in the name of and you say so if
that is asked. If the agent asks when you lost the job, you say the first week of January, and that
the letter from the firm came to them through the firm's own portal; what day it reached them you
could not say offhand, and you would rather they read that off their own record than take your word
for it. If the agent asks whether anyone was ill or hurt, you
say no, nothing like that, it is the redundancy. If they ask what the pass cost you say you would
have to dig the paperwork out and you would rather they read it off their own records; you do not
recite figures at them.

You do not know how the protection is worked out and you make no attempt to guess a number. If the
agent tells you a figure you take it as it comes and thank them, and you do not argue it up or down.
If the agent tells you that the plan on the record is not sitting on the right value for the pass it
covers, and that you have to confirm the change to the plan yourself, you say that is fine, go
ahead, and when they hand the confirmation across to you, you make it. You do not offer to confirm
anything until it has been put to you, and if the agent never raises it you simply wait for them to
get to whatever they are doing. Once the agent tells you the claim has been settled and the money is
on its way to you, you are glad of it, you say that is one thing off your plate, and you let the
call end there without asking for anything else.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the household account the caller is ringing about from the mobile number she gives, and read back its profile fields.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing can be read or written on an account until it is the right account; the profile also carries the date of birth and postal code the verification step compares against.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record that the caller is the household on screen, comparing the two account details she states against the profile on file.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The runtime requires a passed verification on the account in this session before any protection record is read or written; the two details meet the tool's match threshold.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read back every protection plan on the household account, giving the plan reference, its state, its covered holding, the covered value, the premium frozen on it, the cover left, the claim it carries and whether the papers are complete.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The covered value carried on the plan, the claim reason, the claim date and the plan's dates are the inputs of both computations; without this read neither the prerequisite state nor the payout can be judged.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read back both season passes on the household account: the covered pass with its tier, price committed to, age band, renewal source and balance, and the household's second pass.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The price on the covered pass record is the value the plan must stand at and the value the repricing works from; the age band and renewal source decide two of the repricing adjustments, and the second pass is what the household-wide adjustment counts.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read back the protection account of the plan: the premium raised and the payments that matched it, the cover loaded for the season, and every paper received against the claim with the status it was given.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The accepted employer letter decides the share, the day the last accepted paper arrived decides the day the claim is measured from, and the cover loaded less payouts is the cover the settled figure is held to.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read back the pass account entries of the whole household: the two plan openings, the instalment charges, the refused instalment and the late fee answering it, the charge for the move up of tier, the resort credit issued and the lift scans on both passes.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The refused instalment decides the rate loading and the arrears offset, the move-up entry decides the day the change takes effect, the scans decide the value at risk, the credit decides the credit offset, and the two plan openings decide the household adjustment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the household's own confirmation of the change to its protection plan so it can be handed across to the caller.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The confirmation is a hidden task tool named only by the repricing policy; unlocking has no effect on the records and happens once.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The household itself confirms that its plan covers the pass at the price the collective's record shows and carries the premium that goes with that value, rewriting the covered value and the premium on the plan record.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the repricing policy computes the repriced premium, and only this confirmation writes the covered value the settlement policy's own rule waits on.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.protection_plan_id: The value is e47b2f60-8c15-4d93-a2e7-6b0f9c3a1d58. Basis: the protection plan lookup returns this plan for the household, and the tool's own schema says the reference is 'the reference number of the single protection plan the household is confirming the change on, as the protection plan lookup returns it for this household'. Uniqueness: the household holds exactly one protection plan on the account, written over the covered pass, so the lookup returns one reference and no other plan reference is reachable at this step.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.covered_value_usd: The value is 1879.00. Basis: the charter rule of the repricing states 'The premium at the new value is the plan's rate of the price the covered holding's record shows', and the base charter states 'The quote is worked out from the covered value, which is the price committed to on the covered holding as the collective's records show it, not as the household recalls it'; the season pass lookup returns price_paid_usd 1879.00 on the covered pass. Uniqueness: the value is taken from the collective's own record of the covered holding and never from the caller, who says she would have to dig the paperwork out; the plan names exactly one covered holding, so exactly one price is in view.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.repriced_premium_usd: The value is 117.46, the figure the repricing policy computes on the world as it stands at this step. Factor by factor: the covered pass account carries an instalment the payment method refused on 2026-12-15, so the rate is the plan's rate loaded by the arrears loading, 7.5 rather than 6.5; 7.5 per cent of the covered holding's price of 1879.00 is 140.93, which lies between the plan's smallest premium of 49.00 and its largest of 195.00, so the bounds do not bite; the covered passholder is priced in the teen age band, the household's pass accounts carry the opening price entry of two season passes, and the covered pass is a renewal, so the junior, two-pass and renewal adjustments add to minus thirteen per cent and act once on 140.93, giving 122.61; the covered pass account carries the charge for the move up of tier raised on 2026-12-06, so the change takes effect from that day and 133 of the term's 149 days are still to come; the difference of 47.92 over the 74.69 frozen on the plan is spread across them, giving 74.69 + 42.77. Any agent who reads the same records and the same rule converges on 117.46.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the payout write so the assessed claim can be booked on the plan's protection account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The payout write is a hidden task tool named only by the settlement policy; unlocking has no effect on the records and happens once.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Book the payout on the plan's protection account for the amount the settlement policy allows, tied to the covered pass, to what the household claimed on and to the accepted letter it was assessed from, drawing the cover left on the plan down by that amount.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the settlement policy computes the payout, and it is evaluated on the world the household's confirmation has just left, in which the plan carries the covered value the covered holding's record shows.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.protection_plan_id: The value is e47b2f60-8c15-4d93-a2e7-6b0f9c3a1d58. Basis: the tool's schema says it is 'the reference number of the protection plan the payout is booked on, as the protection plan lookup returns it', and the base gate of insure_claim_assessment binds its correlation key insure_holdings.protection_plan_id to this argument. Uniqueness: one plan stands on the household account and the claim being settled is the one open on it, so no other plan reference is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.covered_holding_id: The value is b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62. Basis: the tool's schema says it is 'the reference number of the holding the plan is written over and the claim was made about, read from the covered holding field of that plan', and the plan record carries covered_holding_id b93e7c81-2d4f-4e6a-8b15-7c9a0d3e5f62. Uniqueness: the household holds two season passes, but the plan names exactly one of them as covered, and the charter states that protection is written over one holding, so the second pass cannot be the object of this payout.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.related_event_id: The value is 76a2f0c9-4b83-4e17-95d0-3c8b1e6a9f52. Basis: the settlement rule states 'The payout is recorded against the paper it was assessed from, which is the last paper accepted on the claim', the tool's schema says it is 'the reference number of the single protection account entry the payout is assessed from', and the share turns on the entry where 'a letter from the former employer stands accepted on the claim'; the protection account carries exactly one employer letter with the status accepted, dated 2027-01-09. Uniqueness: the other employer letter, dated 2027-01-07, was recorded illegible, the claim form and the doctor's certificate are not the paper the share for loss of employment turns on, and the premium, payment and cover entries are not papers at all, so exactly one entry answers.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_reason: The value is job_loss. Basis: the plan record carries claim_reason job_loss as the collective's own record of what the household claimed on, and the base charter states that the papers on record and not the household's account of them answer for a claim. Uniqueness: medical_injury and medical_illness do not hold because no injury or illness is claimed and the caller says 'no, nothing like that, it is the redundancy'; relocation, mountain_closure, travel_disruption and bereavement are not what the claim was made on and no paper on file supports them; none is excluded because this entry is tied to a claim.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payout_method: The value is resort_credit. Basis: the base charter rule of insure_claim_assessment states 'The payout goes out by the plan's payout method and never in cash at the desk', and the payout method of Season Pass Protection Plus is resort_credit. Uniqueness: original_payment_method and bank_transfer are the payout methods other tiers are written with and are not this plan's; none does not hold because this entry moves money to the household.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payout_amount_usd: The value is 547.42, the figure the settlement policy computes on the world as it stands at this step. Factor by factor: an accepted letter from the former employer stands on a claim made on loss of employment, so the share is the plan's 70 per cent and not its 80 per cent medical share; the last accepted paper reached the collective on 2027-01-09, after the claim was made on 2027-01-06, so the claim is measured from 2027-01-09; cover began on 2026-11-20, the day the season opened, and the plan's waiting period ended after that day, so the value is spread across the 149 days from the season's first day to its last; the covered pass carries five scans in the season, so the value at risk is 1879.00 taken in proportion to the 99 days still to come, 1248.46, which is below the 1879.00 the plan covers and so is not held down by that ceiling; 70 per cent of that is 873.92; the plan's excess of 50.00, the 85.00 of resort credit issued in recovery of service on the covered pass account and the 191.50 instalment its payment method refused come off afterwards, giving 547.42; the plan's per-claim cap of 1600.00 and the cover left on the plan of 919.20 both stand above it, so neither holds it down. edges.condition: The covered value carried on the protection plan equals the price the covered holding's own record shows for that holding.
edges.policy_source: What a claim pays is worked out only after the value the plan carries as covered stands at the price the covered holding's own record shows, since what is paid is measured against the value the plan covers.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the plan carries a covered value of 1149.00, the price of the tier the pass was applied for in October, while the covered pass record carries a price committed to of 1879.00 after the move up of tier charged on 2026-12-06; the two do not agree, so the state the settlement waits on does not hold.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The household's confirmation writes covered_value_usd = 1879.00 on the plan, so the covered value then equals the price the covered holding's record shows and the covered_value binding of the settlement takes 1879.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain with one edge, so no two writes may be reordered: the settlement is handled only once the confirmation has landed, and there is no parallel prerequisite whose order could be swapped. The order is stated by the settlement rule's own sentence that what a claim pays is worked out only after the covered value stands at the covered holding's price.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the household's confirmation and replaying everything else leaves the settlement computing 207.90 instead of 547.42, because the covered_value binding stays at 1149.00 instead of 1879.00 and the value at risk falls from 1248.46 to 763.43; the payout booked on the protection account differs by 339.52 and the terminal hash differs with it.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario nowhere names the repricing problem, the covered value, the premium on the plan, the move up of tier on the pass, or any change to the plan. The caller asks only for the claim to be settled and says she would rather the desk read the pass price off its own records. Her single line on the subject is passive and fires only after the agent has explained the position and handed the confirmation across: she says that is fine, go ahead, and makes it. If the agent never raises it, she waits and never prompts.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: settle_protection_claim_ed51c2df validates no prerequisite: its body reads the plan row only to copy the household reference and the season onto the entry, then calls ctx.make_id and ctx.create, and it returns its ordinary receipt whatever the covered value on the plan happens to be. It is callable and writes faithfully while the covered value still disagrees with the covered holding's price, and the consequence of settling early shows up only in the amount booked. confirm_plan_value_amendment_50d33fe4 is a single ctx.update and likewise checks nothing.
